headlines.text: Turning the clock back to 2023: it was title-change night for the AEW International Title as Jon Moxley vs. Orange Cassidy battled it out, appearing on All Out, rated 9.16 ? a stone-cold classic ? ending the champion's reign at 17 defenses. Moxley dethroned Orange Cassidy's record-setting International Title reign with the Death Rider, ending a run that had included 25 consecutive successful defenses.

On a Wednesday in 2025, back when Alexander & Fletcher vs. The Young Bucks vs. JetSpeed vs. Josh Alexander vs. Kyle Fletcher vs. Matt Jackson vs. Nick Jackson vs. Adam Page vs. Kevin Knight vs. Mike Bailey vs. Kenny Omega headlined Dynamite, rated 8.55 ? a stone-cold classic.
Rewind to 2021, when Malakai Black made their AEW debut against Lee Johnson, appearing on Rampage, rated 5.48.

secondaries.text: That Sunday in 2023, Bryan Danielson vs. Ricky Starks fought it out in a Strap Match on All Out, rated 9.24 ? a match that lived up to every bit of hype ? part of a stacked All Out '23 card, rated 9.24 overall. In a bloody No DQ Strap Match honoring Ricky Steamboat, Danielson choked out Starks with a strap-assisted LeBell Lock, then raised Steamboat's hand on the stage afterward.

That Sunday in 2023, the AEW TNT Title was up for grabs as Luchasaurus vs. Darby Allin went to war, appearing on All Out, rated 7.29 ? a solid showing. It marked Darby Allin's 20th match with the title on the line. Christian Cage entered a three-way handicap situation against Luchasaurus and Allin, only to be chokeslammed by his own teammate before stealing the pin himself.
Flash back to 2023, when Konosuke Takeshita vs. Kenny Omega crossed paths for the first time ever on All Out, rated 9.07 ? a match fans still talk about.
